findings.title: Hong Kong Monetary Authority and Bank Indonesia Strengthen Cooperation in Cross-Border Payments

rendered_html: 📔 Regulatory Bulletin — 25 September 2026 (Daily) Executive Summary • 🟡 HKMA and Bank Indonesia signed an MoU to explore interoperable QR-code cross-border payments between Hong Kong and Indonesia. It creates no stated participant requirement, implementation arrangement or deadline; monitor only for a later arrangement that defines scope or participation. Hong Kong 🟡 Hong Kong Monetary Authority and Bank Indonesia Strengthen Cooperation in Cross-Border Payments 🇭🇰 Item ID: item-20260924-hkma-press-b4caea60d3 ⏰ Deadline: No source deadline stated Products: Cross-border payments, QR payments, Digital The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) and Bank Indonesia signed a memorandum of understanding on 24 September 2026 to strengthen cooperation on QR-code-based cross-border payments. The authorities say they will hold technical, operational and regulatory dialogues and explore arrangements to facilitate interoperability between Hong Kong and Indonesia. The announcement is prospective and states no rollout, participant requirement, technical standard or compliance deadline. Payment providers and Hong Kong–Indonesia merchants may be affected only if a later arrangement establishes participation or interoperability; current scope remains unstated. Source: Hong Kong Monetary Authority and Bank Indonesia Strengthen Cooperation in Cross-Border Payments Mainland/GBA No validated Mainland/GBA developments in this edition. SG/UK/GLOBAL Benchmark Comparable overseas developments and commercial/control benchmarks. They do not establish Hong Kong requirements. No validated SG/UK/GLOBAL benchmark developments in this edition. Watch List • Monitor for a subsequent HKMA or Bank Indonesia arrangement setting out participating entities, payment-scheme standards, customer protections, approvals or timetable for QR-payment interoperability.
